title: Admission and Assessment Timing Standards — Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement
content:
The Wellness Department and the Admissions Office apply the following figures to the Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement. Day counts are calendar days.

| Standard | Level 1 | Level 2 | Level 3 | Level 4 | Level 5 | Level 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum age of the resident on the move-in date, years | 55 | 55 | 55 | 55 | 55 | 55 |
| Wander or exit-seeking risk excludes assisted living (referral to memory care) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Maximum days between the pre-admission nurse assessment and the move-in date | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Days after the move-in date by which the first reassessment is completed | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |
| Maximum days between routine reassessments at this care level | 180 | 180 | 180 | 120 | 90 | 90 |
| Days after return from a qualifying hospital stay by which a reassessment is completed | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| Midnights in hospital that make an absence a qualifying hospital stay | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Days after an assessment indicating a new level by which the written level notice is issued | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| Days after the written level notice before an increase from a routine or post-move-in reassessment takes effect | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 | 30 |

### Reading the table

- The routine interval is the one figure that differs by level: 180 days at Assisted Living Care Levels 1 to 3, 120 days at Level 4 and 90 days at Levels 5 and 6. The interval applies at the care level billed.
- A hospital absence of 2 midnights or more is a qualifying hospital stay; a hypothetical absence of 1 midnight is not.
